name: NEAR Shoemaker

terrain.note: Microgravity undulating asteroid surface with boulder scree and electrostatic dust ponds

keyDiscovery: First spacecraft to orbit and softly touch down upon an asteroid, returning 160,000 images and discovering micro-impact regolith sorting.
missionLegacy: Proved that low-cost robotic craft could navigate and soft-land in irregular microgravity, founding modern asteroid deflection and planetary defense.

objects.name: NEAR Spacecraft Bus
objects.description: Octagonal aluminum and honeycomb composite bus containing hydrazine propellant tanks and 450 N LEROS bipropellant apogee thruster.
objects.source: NASA NSSDC Master Catalog / JHU APL
objects.scienceDiscovery: Executed a flawless 1.9 m/s controlled descent touchdown onto an uncharted asteroid surface without specialized landing legs.
objects.legacy: Humanity's first robotic footprint resting permanently upon an asteroid.
objects.firstPerson: I am NEAR Shoemaker. After mapping 433 Eros for a year, I descended gently at walking speed to rest upon this primordial space rock.

objects.name: GaAs Solar Array Wings
objects.description: Four 1.8 x 1.2 m fixed gallium arsenide solar panel wings producing 1,800 W at 1.0 AU, canted to capture oblique solar rays.
objects.scienceDiscovery: Maintained continuous electrical bus voltage during surface contact despite extreme low Sun elevation angles.
objects.legacy: Pioneered durable gallium arsenide photovoltaic cells for deep-space missions beyond Earth orbit.
objects.firstPerson: My four solar wings kept me alive millions of kilometers from Earth, soaking in the sunlight of the asteroid belt.

objects.name: Multispectral Imager (MSI)
objects.description: Seven-color framing CCD camera with refractive telephoto optics capable of resolving surface features down to millimeters during descent.
objects.scienceDiscovery: Returned the highest-resolution images ever taken of an asteroid, showing shattered rock fragments and smooth dust ponds.
objects.legacy: Provided ground-truth optical characterization of an S-type near-Earth asteroid.
objects.firstPerson: My eyes captured 160,000 photographs of Eros, snapping my final close-up just 120 meters above the boulders.

objects.name: X-Ray / Gamma-Ray Spectrometer (XGRS)
objects.description: NaI(Tl) scintillation detector and gas proportional counters measuring cosmic-ray-induced fluorescent elemental emissions.
objects.scienceDiscovery: Confirmed Eros is an undifferentiated primitive ordinary chondrite, fundamentally identical to meteorites found on Earth.
objects.legacy: Settled the decades-long scientific dispute connecting S-type asteroids to ordinary chondritic meteorites.
objects.firstPerson: While resting directly on the ground, my gamma-ray sensors sniffed out magnesium, silicon, and iron in the pristine asteroid soil.

objects.name: NEAR Laser Rangefinder (NLR)
objects.description: Diode-pumped Nd:YAG pulsed laser transmitter firing 1,064 nm beams at 8 Hz with a 3.5-inch gold-coated receiver telescope.
objects.scienceDiscovery: Mapped over 11 million laser ranging points to create the first complete 3D global topography model of an asteroid.
objects.legacy: Set the precedent for all future asteroid shape modeling, including OSIRIS-REx and Hayabusa2.
objects.firstPerson: I pulsed green-infrared laser light across canyons and craters to chart every hill and valley on Eros.

objects.name: Eros Regolith Boulder Field
objects.description: Pristine rubble-strewn asteroid terrain composed of ancient chondritic breccia, shattered ejecta blocks, and smooth flat dust ponds.
objects.scienceDiscovery: Revealed electrostatic levitation of ultra-fine dust grains into low depressions without atmosphere or liquid flow.
objects.legacy: Uncovered electrostatic dust transport mechanisms now observed across airless worlds.
objects.firstPerson: We are the primordial boulders of Eros, undisturbed since the formation of the Solar System 4.5 billion years ago.
